title: Options Strategies & Breakevens

sections.heading: Core Vocabulary (memorize)
items: 1 contract = 100 shares; premium quoted per share (× 100 = total $)
Buyer = long, holder, owner, pays premium, has the RIGHT
Seller = short, writer, receives premium, has the OBLIGATION
Calls: Buyer BULLISH / Writer BEARISH
Puts: Buyer BEARISH / Writer BULLISH
Premium = Intrinsic Value + Time Value (IV + TV = Prem)
Time value ↑ with more time to expiration & higher volatility
Equity option exercise settles T+1 (post-5/28/2024); premium trades settle T+1

sections.heading: ITM / ATM / OTM (intrinsic value never negative)
The 4 Basic Positions — BE / MG / ML
Calls BE Mnemonic: 'Call Up' / Puts BE: 'Put Down'
items: Call BE = Strike + Premium (add up)
Put BE  = Strike − Premium (subtract down)
Same BE for buyer & seller — one's MG is the other's ML

sections.heading: Long Straddle (buy 1 call + 1 put, same strike & expiration)
items: Used when expecting BIG MOVE — direction unknown (high volatility play)
Upside BE = Strike + TOTAL premiums (both)
Downside BE = Strike − TOTAL premiums (both)
Max Gain = Unlimited (upside via call)
Max Loss = Total premiums paid (stock stays at strike)
Short Straddle = opposite: profits if stock stays still; UNLIMITED loss potential

rows: Equity options, most equity index options
Foreign currency options, yield-based (interest rate) options

sections.heading: Quick Calc Examples
items: Long 1 XYZ 40 Call @ 3 → BE 43; MG unlimited; ML $300
Short 1 XYZ 40 Call @ 3 → BE 43; MG $300; ML unlimited
Long 1 XYZ 40 Put @ 3 → BE 37; MG $3,700; ML $300
Short 1 XYZ 40 Put @ 3 → BE 37; MG $300; ML $3,700
Long Straddle 50 strike, call 3 + put 2 → BEs 55 & 45; ML $500

sections.heading: Exercise & Expiration Quick Facts
items: Options expire 3rd Friday of expiration month, 11:59 pm ET
Auto-exercise if ITM by ≥ $0.01 at expiration (unless 'do not exercise')
OCC issues, guarantees, and standardizes listed options
Equity option exercise → stock settles T+1 (updated May 2024)

common_traps: Reversing the BE formulas — 'Call Up, Put Down': Calls add premium, Puts subtract premium. Same BE for buyer AND writer.
Forgetting Long Put max gain is NOT unlimited — stock can only fall to $0, so MG = Strike − Premium.
Confusing market attitude: a PUT WRITER is BULLISH (wants stock up/flat); a CALL WRITER is BEARISH. Not the same as the buyer.
Naked CALL writing = unlimited loss; naked PUT writing = large but LIMITED loss (strike − premium). Don't call a short put 'unlimited risk.'
Straddle BE uses the SUM of both premiums (added to strike for upside, subtracted for downside) — not just one premium.
Currency and yield-based options are EUROPEAN style (expiration day only) — easy to mismark as American.
